items.content:
Any domain user. Domain Controller certificate. Full domain compromise. One Python script. Default configuration.

Certighost (CVE-2026-54121, CVSS 8.8) abuses the AD CS enrollment chase fallback. The CA reads an attacker-controlled `cdc` attribute and follows it to a rogue host without ever checking if the target is a real Domain Controller.

Create a machine account via the default MachineAccountQuota. Spin up rogue LDAP and SMB listeners. The CA connects back, authenticates through the real DC via Netlogon, but your rogue LDAP returns the target DC's objectSid and dNSHostName instead. The CA issues a valid Domain Controller certificate.

PKINIT with the DC's PFX. DCSync the entire domain. Extract krbtgt. Game over.

Works with the default Machine template and default ACLs. No special configuration required.

Patched July 14, 2026. PoC dropped yesterday. If your AD CS hosts are not patched, this is your priority.

Temporary mitigation: certutil -setreg policy\EditFlags -EDITF_ENABLECHASECLIENTDC

https://t.co/Cyj7qTXY7V

Authors: @h0j3n @aniqfakhrul

#ActiveDirectory #InfoSec #BlueTeam

items.content:
RT @merill: I recently made a video explaining how Entra Staged Rollout works here https://t.co/D7XbHuCeC3

There's one big change Microsoft made recently (May/June) to this feature and mentioned it was for security. 

My speculation is that a tenant was compromised because someone flipped over the auth flow of global admin (or another privileged) by moving the the account in and out of staged rollout.

It's a neat way to stay hidden. 

But here's a secret. If an account is already in staged roll out you don't need to go through the hard work of changing their groups etc.

Just add the domain's home realm discovery shortcut (?whr=https://t.co/YLtnr1Qwtu). 

With this, even if the account is in PHS with staged rollout you will be taken to the federated identity provider to sign in.

So remember folks, always use a cloud identity for your privileged roles and monitor your federated config. 

You can also protected action but a GA can always turn it off.

PS You can set up montoring for all these key parts of you Entra config with https://t.co/tZHdkWnzP5. 

The best part is the tests are already written. This specific one about cloud admins can be found at https://t.co/QDPPLc5bfl

It's a CIS standard too

Attacker
(low-privileged user)
          |

          v
Starts fake LDAP server
          |

Certificate Authority
          |
          | "I'll contact the

          v
Fake LDAP server
controlled by attacker
          |
          | "Yep, that's DC01"

     ❌!!! VULNERABILITY !!!❌

CA trusts the LDAP response
WITHOUT properly verifying
that it came from the real
Domain Controller.

          |
          v
CA issues a Domain Controller
certificate to the attacker
          |
          v
Attacker authenticates
AS the Domain Controller

items.content:
RT @andersonc0d3: This was fixed after I reported a way to bypass pointer guard (PTR_MANGLE) in glibc. I had known about and taught the technique in my binary exploitation classes for a few years (since ~2020/2021), but I wasn't sure whether the glibc team was aware of it.

After the report, a developer mentioned several related issues and started working on the fixes. Besides the technique I reported, I didn't know about the others — I don't focus on binary exploitation beyond my training classes. I was surprised by how many issues there were in glibc that allowed mitigation bypasses. The fix for one of those issues landed in glibc 2.44 today.
